description: Container platform for packaging, distributing and running isolated applications.

docker-run.title: Run container
docker-run.description: Creates and starts a container from an image, pulling it from the registry if needed.
examples: Runs Docker's test image.
Starts nginx in the background, publishing port 80 on 8080.

docker-ps.title: List containers
docker-ps.description: Lists running containers, with id, image, ports and status.
examples: Shows active containers.
Includes stopped containers.

docker-exec.title: Run command in container
docker-exec.description: Runs a command inside a running container, useful for opening an interactive shell.
examples: Opens a shell inside the web container.
Opens psql inside the database container.

docker-stop.title: Stop container
docker-stop.description: Sends SIGTERM to the container's main process and, after the timeout, SIGKILL, stopping it safely.
examples: Stops the web container.
Stops all running containers.
warnings: Processes that don't handle SIGTERM may lose unsaved data.

docker-rm.title: Remove container
docker-rm.description: Removes one or more stopped containers. Use -f to force removal of running containers.
examples: Removes the stopped web container.
Forces removal of all containers.
warnings: Removing a container deletes its internal filesystem (data outside volumes is lost).

docker-logs.title: View container logs
docker-logs.description: Shows a container's stdout and stderr, useful for debugging.
examples: Shows the web container's logs.
Follows the last 100 lines in real time.
arguments: Shows only the last n lines.

docker-stats.title: Monitor resource usage
docker-stats.description: Shows containers' CPU, memory, network and I/O usage in real time.
examples: Shows resources for all active containers.
Shows a single snapshot, without refreshing.

docker-inspect.title: Inspect object
docker-inspect.description: Returns detailed metadata as JSON for containers, images, volumes or networks.
examples: Shows all metadata of the web container.
Extracts only the IP using a Go template.
arguments: Formats the output with a Go template.

docker-images.title: List images
docker-images.description: Lists locally stored images, with repository, tag, id and size.
examples: Lists local images.

docker-pull.title: Pull image
docker-pull.description: Downloads an image from a registry (Docker Hub by default) for local use.
examples: Pulls the Node 20 image, alpine variant.
warnings: Always pin a specific tag; the latest tag changes over time and breaks reproducibility.

docker-build.title: Build image
docker-build.description: Builds an image from a Dockerfile in the current context, applying a name and tag.
examples: Builds the minha-app:1.0 image using the current Dockerfile.
Multi-stage build targeting the prod stage, with a build argument.
arguments: Builds up to a specific stage (multi-stage).
warnings: Avoid copying sensitive files; use .dockerignore to shrink the context and protect secrets.

docker-tag.title: Tag image
docker-tag.description: Creates a new reference (tag) for an existing image, usually before pushing to a registry.
examples: Prepares the image to push to the private registry.

docker-push.title: Push image to registry
docker-push.description: Pushes a local image to a remote registry, requiring prior login when it is private.
examples: Publishes the image to the registry.
warnings: Make sure the image contains no secrets before publishing it.

docker-login.title: Log in to registry
docker-login.description: Authenticates to the registry to allow pulling and pushing private images.
examples: Logs in to Docker Hub.
Non-interactive login reading the token from standard input.
arguments: Reads the password/token from stdin (avoids exposing it in history).
warnings: Don't pass the password with --password on the command line; it ends up in shell history.

docker-rmi.title: Remove image
docker-rmi.description: Removes one or more local images. Fails if containers are using the image.
examples: Removes the node:18 image.
warnings: Removed images must be pulled or rebuilt again.

docker-volume-create.title: Create volume
docker-volume-create.description: Creates a Docker-managed volume to persist data beyond the container's lifecycle.
examples: Creates the db-data volume.
Mounts the volume at Postgres's data directory.

docker-volume-ls.title: List volumes
examples: Lists all volumes.

docker-network-ls.title: List networks
docker-network-ls.description: Lists Docker networks, including the default ones (bridge, host, none) and custom ones.
examples: Lists the available networks.

docker-network-create.title: Create network
docker-network-create.description: Creates a custom bridge network, letting containers talk to each other by service name.
examples: Creates the app-net network.
Connects the container to the app-net network.

docker-cp.title: Copy files to/from container
docker-cp.description: Copies files or directories between the host and a container.
examples: Copies a file from the container to the host.
Copies from the host to the container.

docker-restart.title: Restart container
docker-restart.description: Stops and starts a container again, applying new host environment variables when needed.
examples: Restarts the web container.

docker-system-df.title: View disk usage
docker-system-df.description: Shows how much space images, containers, volumes and cache are using.
examples: Summary of Docker disk usage.
Breaks it down by image and volume.

docker-image-prune.title: Prune unused images
docker-image-prune.description: Removes dangling images. With -a, removes all images with no associated container.
examples: Removes only dangling images.
Removes all images not used by containers.
warnings: -a removes images you may have to pull again.

docker-system-prune.title: Docker system cleanup
docker-system-prune.description: Removes stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images and, with -a, all unused images.
examples: Basic cleanup of stopped containers and orphaned networks.
Aggressive cleanup including unused images and volumes.
warnings: --volumes deletes persisted data that isn't in use.
Don't use indiscriminately on production servers.

docker-scout.title: Analyze vulnerabilities
docker-scout.description: Scans an image for known vulnerabilities (CVEs), helping with supply chain security.
examples: Lists CVEs found in the image.
